notes: Florida's All-State choruses are run by the Florida Vocal Association (FVA), a component of the Florida Music Education Association (FMEA), and perform at the FMEA Professional Learning Conference. Data below comes from the All-State Omnibus 2026-2027 (revised 7/14/2026), the current-cycle governing document. Note that fva.net/all-state was still displaying the prior (2026) cycle's announced excerpts when retrieved, so no 2027 announced VQ excerpts are recorded here. FEMEA (Florida Elementary Music Educators Association) separately runs a 2027 All-State Elementary Chorus, included as its own program. The FEMEA page publishes its deadlines as month/day only (9/12, 9/24, 10/15, 10/23, 11/3); the calendar year 2026 is taken from the cycle context (fall before the January 2027 conference).

organization.name: Florida Vocal Association
organization.description: FVA is the choral component of the Florida Music Education Association. Its All-State Choruses are select groups of choral students from Florida's junior, middle, and senior high schools who complete a three-step audition process (written musicianship test, sight-reading, and a vocal quality audition on the All-State music) and then rehearse and perform with guest conductors at the annual FMEA Professional Learning Conference.

programs.name: All-State High School Concert Chorus
programs.description: Approximately 300 singers, grades 9-12, SATB. Seated with the highest 75 composite scores per SATB voice part (37 in part 1 of each section, 38 in part 2). Rehearses and performs at the FMEA Professional Learning Conference. 2027 conductor: Chris Maunu.

requirements.title: Eligibility
requirements.description: Students in grades 7-12 who are enrolled in a choral/vocal course at their school or a registered Home Education Music Cooperative are eligible to audition for an All-State ensemble. The Concert Chorus is grades 9-12.

requirements.title: Three-step audition process
requirements.description: 1) 50-question multiple-choice written musicianship test, graded on-site; 2) individual sight-reading evaluation scored by two approved choral directors on the number of correct measures sung; 3) a Vocal Quality Audition on the All-State music. Composite scores are 30% musicianship, 35% sight-reading, 35% vocal quality.

requirements.title: Qualifying scores for the Concert Chorus
requirements.description: Students must score at least 80% (40/50) on the 9-12 Musicianship Test and correctly read a minimum of 20 measures of the 40-measure Sight-Reading Examination in order to complete the Vocal Quality audition for the Concert Chorus.

requirements.title: Vocal Quality Audition repertoire
requirements.description: Students audition on three excerpts selected from the Concert Chorus repertoire; two of the three are discovered on-site at the Vocal Quality Audition and one is announced on fva.net on September 19. Students must prepare the voice part for which they were registered. Learning tracks for all repertoire are available for purchase from ChoralTracks.

requirements.title: Registration limits and voice part locking
requirements.description: Registration is via MPA Online. Each director may register a maximum of 3 students each of Soprano 1, Soprano 2, Alto 1, and Alto 2; there is no limit on Tenors and Basses. Students must register for the voice part for which they wish to be considered (S1, S2, A1, A2, T1, T2, B1, B2) and may not change voice parts after the registration deadline. Directors also supply emergency contact information, height, and a student headshot at registration.

requirements.title: Testing accommodations
requirements.description: A director may request visual magnification, preferential seating, or Braille for students with special needs, with ample prior notification to the district chair.

requirements.title: Opt-out procedure
requirements.description: Directors may opt students on the lower edge of the Concert Chorus audition pool out of Concert Chorus so they instead audition on the SSAA or TTBB packet. Once a student is moved out of the Concert Chorus pool they cannot be moved back, regardless of score.

fees.description: A minimum $25.00 audition fee is charged for each student registered to take the musicianship test. Only school or booster checks, money orders, or credit cards are accepted; personal checks, cash, and purchase orders are not. No refunds for students who do not show up. Districts may elect to add an additional recording fee.

programs.name: All-State High School Reading Chorus
programs.description: Approximately 100 singers, grades 9-12; members are the highest sight-reading scorers in the state. This is the first chorus seated, awarded after the musicianship and sight-reading exams and before the Vocal Quality audition. 2027 conductor: Dr. Erynn M. Millard.

dates.title: FMEA Professional Learning Conference and All-State Concerts

requirements.title: Seating criteria
requirements.description: Unless a student opts out, the top 25 sight readers in each section (SATB) are awarded the 100 Reading Chorus seats. The minimum sight-reading score accepted is 30 measures out of 40, and Reading Chorus members must have a minimum score of 40 on the Musicianship exam. Seats are awarded before the Vocal Quality audition. Directors indicate at initial online registration which students want to opt out of Reading Chorus consideration.

programs.name: All-State Elementary Chorus
programs.description: Administered by FEMEA (the Florida Elementary Music Educators Association), a component of FMEA. Teachers select students to audition for All-State, Regionals, or both. Auditions are submitted as recordings judged from an official audition track. FEMEA labels this cycle the '2027 All-State Elementary Chorus'.
